plan: This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with a second-price payment rule (Vickrey auction). In such an auction, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Bidding less risks losing to a lower bid, and bidding more risks overpaying if you win. Since this is the first round and there's no history, I'll stick to the dominant strategy.

I will bid slightly above my private value to maximize profit. Since the payment is the second-highest bid, bidding my value guarantees profit if I win, but bidding slightly higher increases my chances of winning without significantly increasing the payment if I do win. I will bid $13.1, slightly above my value.

My value is $17. I'm in a second-price auction, so bidding my true value is generally optimal to maximize expected profit. This strategy ensures I win when my value is higher than the second-highest bid and I don't overpay.
